name: Highlake
description:
The Elves are vague on why they left their ancestral forests. Some say that deceit and betrayal poisoned the roots of their happiness there. Others say that the wilds became too wild under some dark influence. What is certain is that they wandered long and, in time, came to a clear, glassy lake, high in the mountains, and there ceased to wander.

Here they wrought halls and spires in imitation of the great trees that had been the cradles of their ancestors. Their King opened his coffers and the lake soon reflected many flourishes of gold and precious stones on its placid waters. They built walls also: some would say to frame their artful city, others would say to keep out the world. Regardless of their intent, the world soon came knocking.

Fleeing enslavement by a cruel Djinn-Lord in the mountains, great numbers of Orcs gathered outside the walls. They were as loathe to seek help from the Elves as the Elves were to yield it at first - their ancestors having been sworn enemies long ago - but in time each found the other gentler than their old tales would have them believe. When the Djinn-Lord brought a great host against the city, the Orcs swore an oath of alliance with the Elves, and together they routed the invaders, though the Djinn-Lord struck the Elf King dead in the battle. In the aftermath, under the wise leadership of the King's twin daughters, the Elves opened their gates. Soon many red Orcish yurts complimented the green and gold spires of the Elves, and the artwork of the city was complete.

As their peoples mixed, they found their skills in smithing to be highly complimentary. The Queens erected public forges and delved mines into the surrounding mountains to feed them. So Highlake has become a great center of smithcraft and commerce pours in from every quarter. But even as the city prospers, a darkness lingers on the royal house, and it is said that the Queens spend long hours in their high towers sharpening their minds and magics, their thoughts bent on revenge against the Djinn-Lord. While their thrones go unattended, corruption and ambition have begun to take root around them...
